observation_summary: Multiple tests expect primitive double default values (0.0) but actual returns are integer 0 or a ClassCastException (Integer cannot be cast to Double). Tests show assertions expecting 0.0D but receiving 0 (Integer) and one failure shows a ClassCastException from Integer to Double.
reasoning_summary: The failing tests indicate the component that supplies default primitive values is returning the wrong numeric type/value for double (an Integer/0 instead of a Double/0.0). This is a wrong value/type assignment rather than a missing guard, concurrency issue, interface mismatch, or higher-level design omission. The fix would be to assign/initialize the correct Double/0.0 value for double primitive return cases, which matches the Assignment/Initialization category.
evidence_used: Stack trace excerpt: java.lang.ClassCastException: class java.lang.Integer cannot be cast to class java.lang.Double
Test assertion failures: expected:<0.0> but was:<0>
evidence_gaps: No production code snippet showing the method that returns default values (exact return statement or assignment is not provided).
No stack trace frames pointing to the exact file/line of the faulty assignment.
No pre-fix diff or commentary describing the implementation that produced Integer for double.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The failures show a wrong value/type is produced, not merely a missing guard or boundary check. While a missing type-specific branch could be considered a checking issue, the core problem is the incorrect value being returned/assigned for double, which aligns better with Assignment/Initialization.
There is no evidence of an incorrect algorithmic procedure (loops, search, ordering). The issue is about returning the wrong literal/boxed-number type, not a procedural logic error.
This is not a boundary or contract mismatch between modules; tests call an API and receive an incorrect value type from the same component.
No concurrency, ordering, or serialization concerns are indicated by the evidence.
There is no sign of broken associations between related data structures or procedures; the symptom is a single component returning an incorrect value.
The capability to return defaults exists; it is implemented but returns the wrong numeric type/value. This is not a missing or large design-level capability.
